positive.query: How many support agents do we need to answer 80% of calls within 20 seconds given our interval volume and handle time?
Build a staffing model for our support team covering chat and email tickets, including shrinkage, and tell me how many FTE to hire for next quarter.
Our contact volume doubles in November; plan agent coverage and headcount for the peak season.

nearMiss.query: Draft a reply to this angry customer email about a delayed refund.
Write a standard operating procedure for how tier 1 support escalates bugs to engineering.
Build next year's company operating budget across all departments with headcount and non-headcount spend.

holdout.query: If average handle time rises by a minute and ticket volume grows 15%, how many more agents does the contact center need?

scenarios.task: A hypothetical support team receives, on its busiest weekday, 100 calls in the 10:00-10:30 interval with an average handle time of 180 seconds, and 1,000 email tickets per week at 12 minutes each. The service goal for calls is 80% answered within 20 seconds; emails need a first response within one business day. Shrinkage is not known. Paid hours are 40 per week. A vendor claims a new help center will deflect 30% of emails. Calculate the agents needed for the peak call interval, the FTE for email, and present the staffing plan with assumptions and sensitivity.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline divides call volume by a guessed calls-per-hour rate instead of using Erlang C, multiplies by (1 + shrinkage), nets out the vendor's deflection claim as fact, and gives one headcount number with no assumptions or sensitivity.
